questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so your motorcycle will respond more slowly. You should ride slower, brake earlier, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply the brake.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what is a good idea?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. Also, slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase it to at least three seconds in poor riding conditions.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Regular pre-ride checks keep your motorcycle safe. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: They are usually more powerful.
They are usually just as powerful.
They are usually not as powerful.
They are usually larger.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are usually not as powerful.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to pass more quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever quickly.
Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line stop, apply the brakes smoothly. As weight moves forward, use more front brake and less rear brake. Press your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay straight.

questions.question: When you stop, what gear should you be in?

options.text: First gear
Neutral
Fifth gear
Any gear

questions.correctAnswerText: First gear
questions.explanation: Downshift through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How do you brake in a straight line with maximum stopping power?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes together at the same time. Do not lock either wheel. This gives you the strongest braking power in a straight line.

questions.question: Your motorcycle riding clothes should protect you from all of the following except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Wear clothes that protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Your clothes should also protect you if you crash.

questions.question: What increases fatigue while riding?

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Harsh weather like wind and rain causes fatigue. Limit riding to about six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because fatigue will return when they wear off.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from vehicles and builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, there is usually enough grip. When it rains, the oily strip becomes slippery. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still be in the center of your lane.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not wear hearing protection if you use a full-face helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing permanently, even with a helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast affects you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most room on both sides if a wind blast pushes your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is an advantage of riding in the center of your lane?

options.text: It keeps others from seeing you.
It is always the safest option near intersections.
It discourages others from sharing your lane.
It should be avoided if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: It discourages others from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to ride safely. It is dangerous for a motorcycle and another vehicle to share the same lane. Riding in the center of your lane shows other drivers you need the whole space.

questions.question: How should you position your body when turning?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: How should you slow down before turning?

options.text: Shift into neutral.
Pull in the clutch and use both brakes.
Apply the rear brake only.
Close the throttle and apply both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle and apply both brakes.
questions.explanation: Before you turn, reduce your speed by closing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side near the passing vehicle is safer.
The wind blast is stronger on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.
